stemBlocks.value: A triangular field LMP on horizontal ground has LM = 120 m, LP = 150 m and PM = 180 m, with a north line drawn at L. (i) Calculate angle MLP. (ii) The bearing of P from L is 210 degrees. (a) Find the bearing of M from L. (b) Calculate angle NLP and hence find the bearing of L from P.
Think first: All three sides are known, so the angle at L comes from the cosine rule; after that the whole question is about turning angles into compass directions.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p272-q07 from workbook page 272.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the cosine rule for the angle at L using the three sides.

contentBlocks.value: cos(MLP) = (LP squared + LM squared - PM squared) / (2 x LP x LM) = (22500 + 14400 - 32400) / (2 x 150 x 120)
The positive cosine tells you the angle is acute.

solutionSteps.instruction: For (ii)(a), start from the bearing of P and turn back towards M.

contentBlocks.value: In the diagram M lies clockwise of north but anticlockwise of P, so the bearing of M from L = 210 - 82.8
Result: Bearing of M from L = 127.2, i.e. 127 degrees

solutionSteps.instruction: For (ii)(b), find the geometric angle NLP between the north line at L and the line LP.

contentBlocks.value: A bearing of 210 degrees is measured clockwise from north, so the angle you actually draw from the north ray round to LP is 360 - 210 = 150 degrees on the anticlockwise side.

solutionSteps.instruction: Use the parallel north lines at L and P to get the back bearing.

contentBlocks.value: The north line at P is parallel to the north line at L, so the bearing of L from P = 210 - 180.
Result: Bearing of L from P = 030 degrees

strategyBlocks.value: Rearrange the cosine rule to find angle MLP from the three sides, then subtract that angle from the bearing of P to reach M, and use the fact that the north lines at L and P are parallel to get the back bearing.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) angle MLP = 82.8 degrees  (ii)(a) The bearing of M from L is 127 degrees  (ii)(b) angle NLP = 150 degrees and the bearing of L from P is 030 degrees.

whyThisWorks.value: The cosine rule is the only rule that connects three sides to an angle, and rearranging it isolates the cosine of the angle you want. Bearings are directions measured clockwise from north, so any two directions from the same point differ by the angle between them; that is why subtracting angle MLP from the bearing of P gives the bearing of M. Back bearings differ by 180 degrees because the north lines at any two points on a plan are parallel, so the two bearings are co-interior angles across the line joining them.

commonErrors.misconception: Putting the side opposite the required angle in the wrong place in the cosine rule.

commonErrors.misconception: Adding angle MLP to 210 degrees, which would put M in the wrong quadrant.

examTip.value: Bearings are always written with three figures, so 30 degrees must be recorded as 030 degrees.
